# Naming conventions

Following these naming conventions for work by the South East D&A team will make it easy to identify repositories that are ours, and where they sit.

![](pics/wow-naming-conventions.png)

# Where to Clone Repositories

Repositories need to be cloned to personal areas. Cloning a repo creates a local copy of a remote repo and should only be for you to access.

## Acceptable Locations
- Your personal OneDrive
- Your user area within C: drive in UDAL e.g. C:\Users\your.username
- Your Databricks personal workspace

## Unacceptable Locations
- SharePoint
- Shared workspace in Databricks

# Project Structure

Each project/piece of analysis should have:  

- GitHub Repository for code and SOP
- SharePoint folder for other project files i.e. no code

To make it clear where to find each of these:  

- Add a shortcut link to the GitHub Repo in the SharePoint folder (1). (If accessing SharePoint in the file explorer then use shortcut instead (2))

![](pics/wow-shortcut.png)

- Within the GitHub repo README file, add the SharePoint folder path from “Analysis/” onwards. No links please (for security)!

## Where to store reference data/lookups/config files needed to use the repository

### SharePoint
- A copy of the config file required for the code in the repo to run.

A config file contains file paths to data and any other “secrets” e.g. details of the UDAL warehouse server name that are needed for the code to run but cannot be shared for data protection/information governance reasons.

### SE Analytics Lake Mart in UDAL  
- Reference data/lookups not available in the data lake/warehouse
- Any cuts of data specific to that project

## Output of the repository

Outputs should be stored on SharePoint once QA'd.
